chapter_title: Open File Formats and Version Control
learning_objective: The learner will apply the ten editable source checks and the Chapter 3 scoring rules to choose the metric score for each of five resources, with at least 4 of 5 scores exactly correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** editable-source-metric-scorer
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** apply
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply the ten editable source checks and the Chapter 3 scoring rules to choose the metric score for each of five resources, with at least 4 of 5 scores exactly correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** The Editable Source Metric, Metric Score, Scoring Descriptor, Source Format, Open File Format, Changelog (all defined in this chapter or in Chapter 3 above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each resource the learner chooses a whole-number score from 0 to 10 after seeing the ten check results. A score is correct when it equals the Correct score column in Content. Mastery is at least 4 of 5 scores correct on the first attempt. Opening the check list and the descriptor table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Any failed check lowers the score by the same amount. (2) A resource with some editable files scores at least 5. (3) The higher number in a band is always correct. **Instructional Rationale:** Applying a scoring procedure to new cases is an Apply-level task. Five resources with different mixes of passes and blocking failures make the learner use every step: count, band, then choose within the band. **Content:** The ten checks, each marked as blocking or not: | # | Check | Blocks revision if it fails? | |---|---|---| | 1 | An editable source file is offered, not only a PDF | Yes | | 2 | The source is in an open format | Yes | | 3 | The source holds all of the content | Yes | | 4 | The source can be downloaded with no login or payment | Yes | | 5 | Images have their original or vector source files | No | | 6 | Interactive parts supply their code | Yes | | 7 | A short note explains how the pieces fit together | No | | 8 | A record of changes is available | No | | 9 | The reviewer opened the source in a free tool and it displayed correctly | Yes | | 10 | Editing needs no paid software or special template | Yes | The descriptor bands, applied to the share of checks passed: 0% is 0; 1% to 24% is 1 to 2; 25% to 49% is 3 to 4; 50% to 74% is 5 to 6; 75% to 89% is 7 to 8; 90% to 100% is 9 to 10. Within a two-number band, choose the lower number when any failed check blocks revision, and the higher number otherwise. A score of 10 requires every check to pass. A check that does not apply counts as passed. The five resources: | # | Resource | Checks failed | Checks passed | Share | Band | Blocking failure? | Correct score | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Open Algebra | None | 10 | 100% | 9 to 10 | No | 10 | Every check passed, so the score is 10. | | 2 | Watershed Basics | 5 and 8 | 8 | 80% | 7 to 8 | No | 8 | Neither failed check blocks revision, so the higher number applies. | | 3 | District Unit | 3 and 7 | 8 | 80% | 7 to 8 | Yes, check 3 | 7 | The source is missing part of the content, which blocks revision, so the lower number applies. | | 4 | Handout Scans | 1, 2, 3, 5, 9 | 5 (checks 4, 6, 7, 8, 10) | 50% | 5 to 6 | Yes | 5 | Check 6 does not apply and counts as passed. Several blocking checks failed, so the lower number applies. | | 5 | PDF-Only Report | 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9 | 3 (checks 4, 6, 10) | 30% | 3 to 4 | Yes | 3 | Check 6 does not apply and counts as passed. Blocking checks failed, so the lower number applies. | **Provenance:** The ten checks and the descriptor bands follow the chapter sections "The Editable Source Metric" and Chapter 3. The five resources are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". Resource 2 is the chapter's worked example. **Rules:** A score is the band chosen from the share passed, and then the number chosen within the band by the blocking rule. Each resource has exactly one correct score. For a band that holds a single number, that number is the score. **Learner Activity:** 1. The sim shows resource 1 with its ten check results. 2. The learner may open the check list and the descriptor table. 3. The learner chooses a score from 0 to 10, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows the count of passes, the band, whether any failure blocks revision, and the correct score with the Why text. 5. After resource 5 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 5 resources in the fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [score]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. [passes] checks passed, which is [share] and the [band] band. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 5 correct on the first attempt". At 4 or more it adds "You can score editable source." Below 4 it lists the Why text of each missed resource. **Starting State:** Resource 1 with all ten results shown and no score chosen. The question shown is "What editable source score does this resource earn?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked example for Watershed Basics fails checks 5 and 8, passes 8 of 10, and scores 8, with the higher number chosen because neither failure blocks revision.
